name: sf-mcp-server

tools.name: soql_query
tools.description: Query records (data) with SOQL. For schema — what fields an object has — use describe_object. For Apex, Flows and other metadata use list_metadata or list_apex_classes. Consumes one API call per page, and one extra call when resuming a cursor. Returns at most one budget-bounded page: 200 rows by default, 2000 hard maximum, and fewer when the response budget bites first. meta.truncation says exactly how many rows were withheld. Before paging, narrow: add a WHERE clause, select fewer fields, or ask the org to do the work with COUNT() or GROUP BY. An aggregate query answers "how many" in one row instead of fifty thousand. Values must be passed in `binds` as :name placeholders; string concatenation is rejected. INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/UPSERT/MERGE/UNDELETE and FOR UPDATE are rejected with SOQL_REJECTED naming the token and its position — fix the query rather than retrying it. If no org is authenticated this returns NO_ORGS_AUTHENTICATED; tell the user to run `sf org login web --alias <name>`.

soql.description: A SOQL SELECT statement. Use :name placeholders for every value and pass them in `binds`. Exactly one statement; no comments; no FOR UPDATE.

binds.description: Values for the :name placeholders in `soql`. An array becomes an IN list. A string that is exactly an ISO-8601 date (2026-01-01) or datetime (2026-01-01T00:00:00Z) is written as a SOQL date literal, unquoted, which is what a date or datetime field requires; every other string is quoted. Every placeholder must have a bind and every bind must have a placeholder, or the query is rejected without partial substitution.

maxRows.description: Row cap for this page. Default 200, hard ceiling 2000; larger values are clamped, not refused. The response budget often stops the page before this does.

cursor.description: Continuation token from a previous call’s meta.truncation.cursor. Only valid for the same org and the same arguments, and it expires after 15 minutes. Narrowing the request is almost always better than paging.

targetOrg.description: Org alias or username. Defaults to the server’s --target-org, then to the Salesforce CLI target-org. An alias that is not authenticated is an error; it never falls back to the default org.

tools.name: describe_object
tools.description: Describe an object’s schema: its fields, types and relationships. For the records themselves use soql_query; for Apex, Flows and other metadata use list_metadata. Consumes one API call. Returns a bounded page. By default it returns a shape — object facts, a count of fields by type, and a ranked field list (identity and required fields first, audit fields last) with the picklist value COUNT rather than the values. On a 900-field object, do not page and do not pass verbose. Pass fieldFilter with a substring or a glob (for example "Status" or "*__c") to get the few fields you need; that is one call instead of thirty. Use verbose only for the fields fieldFilter has already narrowed to, since it is what returns picklist values. An object that does not exist, or that the user cannot see, returns UPSTREAM_ERROR naming it; check the spelling and the API name (custom objects end in __c) rather than retrying.

object.description: API name of the object, for example Account or Invoice__c. Case-insensitive.

fieldFilter.description: Keep only fields whose API name or label matches. A plain string is a case-insensitive substring; a string containing * or ? is a glob. This is the cheap path — prefer it over paging.

verbose.description: Return the org’s full field records, including picklist values, instead of the ranked summary. Default false. Combine with fieldFilter; verbose without a filter on a large object will be truncated after a handful of fields.

cursor.description: Continuation token from a previous call’s meta.truncation.cursor. Only valid for the same org and the same arguments, and it expires after 15 minutes. Narrowing the request is almost always better than paging.

targetOrg.description: Org alias or username. Defaults to the server’s --target-org, then to the Salesforce CLI target-org. An alias that is not authenticated is an error; it never falls back to the default org.

tools.name: list_metadata
tools.description: List metadata components — Apex classes, Flows, custom objects, layouts, permission sets — by type. For records (data) use soql_query; for an object’s fields use describe_object; for Apex classes specifically list_apex_classes is cheaper and returns sizes. Consumes one API call per three types requested, and caches each type for five minutes, so asking for the same type again in the same session is free. Returns one budget-bounded page. meta.truncation says how many components were withheld and gives a cursor. Narrow before you page: namePattern accepts a substring or a glob (for example "Account*"), and modifiedSince accepts an ISO-8601 timestamp so you can ask only for what changed. On a 10,000-component org these turn thirty pages into one. Ask for at most 10 types in one call; more than that is refused rather than truncated, because a truncated type list reads as though those types are empty. An unknown metadata type returns UPSTREAM_ERROR naming it — check the type’s spelling in the Metadata API (for example ApexClass, not ApexClasses).

types.description: Metadata API type names, for example ["ApexClass", "Flow"]. At most 10 per call; each three types cost one API call.

namePattern.description: Keep only components whose fullName matches. A plain string is a case-insensitive substring; a string containing * or ? is a glob. Prefer this over paging.

modifiedSince.description: ISO-8601 timestamp, for example 2026-01-31T00:00:00Z. Keeps components modified after it. A component whose modification date the org did not report is kept, not dropped — absence of a date is not evidence of no change.

cursor.description: Continuation token from a previous call’s meta.truncation.cursor. Only valid for the same org and the same arguments, and it expires after 15 minutes. Narrowing the request is almost always better than paging.

targetOrg.description: Org alias or username. Defaults to the server’s --target-org, then to the Salesforce CLI target-org. An alias that is not authenticated is an error; it never falls back to the default org.

tools.name: retrieve_metadata
tools.description: Retrieve metadata source — Apex bodies, Flow XML, object definitions — from the org. To find out what exists first, use list_metadata or list_apex_classes; this tool returns file content and is much more expensive. To understand a Flow, use explain_flow instead: it returns a numbered step list rather than several hundred lines of XML. Consumes one API call, plus disk under the server’s --project-dir. Returns at most 25 components. By default (asFiles: true) it writes them under .sf-mcp/retrieved and returns paths and byte sizes, which is small and stays small. Prefer the default and read the one file you need. asFiles: false inlines the source into this response and is capped per component; a component too large to inline is returned as a byte range with a cursor, never as a half file. A component the org does not have is reported in `missing` with the org’s reason rather than failing the call, so one bad name does not cost you the other twenty-four. A path outside the project directory returns PATH_OUTSIDE_PROJECT naming the directory this server is confined to.

type.description: Metadata API type, for example ApexClass.

fullName.description: Component API name, for example AccountService.

components.description: Components to retrieve. At most 25 per call. Get the names from list_metadata rather than guessing them.

asFiles.description: Write to disk and return paths (default, true), or inline the source into this response (false). Inlining is capped per component and will truncate; only use it when you need the text immediately and know the component is small.

cursor.description: Continuation token from a previous call’s meta.truncation.cursor. Only valid for the same org and the same arguments, and it expires after 15 minutes. Narrowing the request is almost always better than paging.

targetOrg.description: Org alias or username. Defaults to the server’s --target-org, then to the Salesforce CLI target-org. An alias that is not authenticated is an error; it never falls back to the default org.

tools.name: diff_orgs
tools.description: Compare metadata between two orgs — what exists in one and not the other, and what has been modified. For a single org’s inventory use list_metadata; this makes two orgs’ worth of calls. Consumes one API call per three types, per org, and caches each org’s listing for five minutes. Returns one budget-bounded page of differences; components identical in both are reported as a count, not a list. Default mode "presence" compares existence and lastModifiedDate and is O(n) — use it first. Note that a differing lastModifiedDate means the component was saved, not necessarily that its content changed; mode "content" retrieves and hashes to answer that, and is capped at 200 components. Above that cap the call is refused with RESULT_TOO_LARGE rather than truncated, because a shortened diff reads as a complete one. Narrow with types or namePattern and run it again. A cursor from one org pair cannot be used for another: it returns CURSOR_ORG_MISMATCH.

sourceOrg.description: Alias or username of the org treated as the source. Must be authenticated.

targetOrg.description: Alias or username of the org compared against. Must be authenticated.

types.description: Metadata API type names to compare, for example ["ApexClass", "Flow"]. At most 10; each three cost one API call per org.

mode.description: "presence" (default) compares existence and lastModifiedDate, is O(n) and needs no retrieve. "content" retrieves both sides and compares hashes, and is refused above 200 components.

namePattern.description: Keep only components whose fullName matches. Substring, or a glob when it contains * or ?. This is how you bring a content diff under the cap.

cursor.description: Continuation token from a previous call’s meta.truncation.cursor. Only valid for the same org and the same arguments, and it expires after 15 minutes. Narrowing the request is almost always better than paging.

tools.name: list_apex_classes
tools.description: List Apex classes in an org with their names and sizes. To read a class body use retrieve_metadata for the specific class; this tool never returns source, because a 5,000-class org is tens of megabytes of it. Consumes one API call per page. Returns at most one budget-bounded page — 200 classes by default, 2000 maximum — with meta.truncation stating how many were withheld. Cheaper path: pass namePattern or modifiedSince so the org filters instead of paging. A plain substring is pushed into the query as a LIKE; a glob is applied here, so a substring is the cheaper of the two. includeBodyStats adds length, API version and status at the cost of a wider row, which means fewer classes fit per page — leave it off unless you need those numbers. An invalid modifiedSince is rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the expected format rather than being silently ignored.

namePattern.description: Keep only classes whose name matches. A plain substring is filtered by the org (cheap); a pattern containing * or ? is treated as a glob and filtered here after fetching.

modifiedSince.description: ISO-8601 timestamp, for example 2026-01-31T00:00:00Z. Filtered by the org, so this is the cheapest way to narrow "what changed recently".

includeBodyStats.description: Include length, apiVersion and status. Widens each row and so reduces how many classes fit in a page. Default false.

maxRows.description: Class cap for this page. Default 200, ceiling 2000; larger values are clamped rather than refused.

cursor.description: Continuation token from a previous call’s meta.truncation.cursor. Only valid for the same org and the same arguments, and it expires after 15 minutes. Narrowing the request is almost always better than paging.

targetOrg.description: Org alias or username. Defaults to the server’s --target-org, then to the Salesforce CLI target-org. An alias that is not authenticated is an error; it never falls back to the default org.

tools.name: explain_flow
tools.description: Explain what a Flow does as an ordered, numbered list of steps. Use this instead of retrieve_metadata for a Flow: the XML is mostly canvas coordinates and connector ids, and this returns the logic without them. Consumes one API call when given flowName, and none when given xml you already have. Returns one budget-bounded page of steps with meta.truncation stating how many were withheld, plus a count of steps the flow’s start element cannot reach. Cheaper path: if you already retrieved the flow, pass its XML as `xml` and this makes no API call at all. Malformed XML is rejected with FLOW_PARSE_FAILED naming where parsing stopped, rather than returning a partial walk. An element type this server does not recognise is reported as "Unknown: <type>" and kept in the sequence, never silently dropped — so a step you do not recognise in the output is a gap in this tool, not in the flow. Passing neither xml nor flowName, or both, is rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

flowName.description: API name of the flow to retrieve and explain, for example "Opportunity_Approval". Mutually exclusive with xml. Costs one API call.

xml.description: Flow metadata XML you already have. Mutually exclusive with flowName. Free — no API call is made.

cursor.description: Continuation token from a previous call’s meta.truncation.cursor. Only valid for the same org and the same arguments, and it expires after 15 minutes. Narrowing the request is almost always better than paging.

targetOrg.description: Org alias or username. Defaults to the server’s --target-org, then to the Salesforce CLI target-org. An alias that is not authenticated is an error; it never falls back to the default org.

tools.name: org_limits
tools.description: Report an org’s governor limits — API requests, storage, async jobs — and how much of each is consumed. For a live view without a tool call, read the org://limits resource instead; it is the same data and the cheaper path when you only want to look. Consumes no daily API requests: the /limits endpoint is exempt. Results are cached for 60 seconds and a repeat call inside that window makes no request at all. Returns one budget-bounded page sorted most-consumed first, so if it is truncated what survives is what is closest to breaking. DailyApiRequests is always included regardless of the sort. Cheaper path when you want one number: pass `filter` with a substring such as "Api" or "Storage" rather than reading the whole list. nearlyExhausted names every limit at or above 95% consumed — relay those to the user, because a job that fails on limits fails without a useful error. Fails with ORG_NOT_FOUND when the alias is not an authenticated org; fix it by running `sf org login web` or passing an alias from `sf org list`.

filter.description: Case-insensitive substring of the limit name, for example "Api" or "Storage". Cheaper than reading every limit and then ignoring most of them.

targetOrg.description: Org alias or username. Defaults to the server’s --target-org, then to the Salesforce CLI target-org. An alias that is not authenticated is an error; it never falls back to the default org.

tools.name: get_deploy_status
tools.description: Report the status of a single deployment by id, including why it failed. For the recent deploy history without an id, read the org://deploy-history resource — that is the cheaper way to find the id to pass here. Consumes one API call. Returns a budget-bounded page: failures first, component failures before the test failures they usually cause, and successful components as a count rather than a list. If the page is truncated, what was withheld is always the tail of the failure list. Cheaper path: check meta.truncation before asking for more — a deploy with three errors returns all three in the first page, and paging is only needed for deploys that failed in bulk. An id that is not a deploy id is rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT before any call is made; an id the org does not know returns NOT_FOUND naming the org it was looked up in, because the usual cause is the right id against the wrong org.

deployId.description: The deployment id, 15 or 18 characters beginning 0Af. From org://deploy-history, or from the output of `sf project deploy start`.

cursor.description: Continuation token from a previous call’s meta.truncation.cursor. Only valid for the same org and the same arguments, and it expires after 15 minutes. Narrowing the request is almost always better than paging.

targetOrg.description: Org alias or username. Defaults to the server’s --target-org, then to the Salesforce CLI target-org. An alias that is not authenticated is an error; it never falls back to the default org.

instructions:
Org: none resolved yet. The first tool call will resolve one, or tell you how to authenticate.
Read-only tools are enabled. Not registered (side-effecting): deploy_validate, run_apex_tests — restart with --allow-write. Not registered (mutating): dml_records, execute_anonymous_apex — restart with --allow-write --allow-mutating.
Every list is one bounded page (~6000 tokens); narrow your filter before you page, and check meta.truncation on every result.
